description:
FILED s470bj from a #996-A3 licence probe (it had to prove a read-only array can
never reach `%p-push1`; it cannot -- the call receives `@a` whole, so #1140's
escape fact keeps `p-push-impl`).  The divergence found on the way is
PRE-EXISTING and unrelated: identical on `e73038f` and identical under
`PCL_OPT=none`.

REPRODUCER (scratch/s470bj/probe/ro2.pl):

    my @a=(1,2);
    print "A", scalar(@a), "\n";
    Internals::SvREADONLY(@a,1);
    print "B", scalar(@a), "\n";

    perl 5.40.3   A2 / B2
    PCL           A2 / B12      <-- "12" is the two ELEMENTS printed, not a count

So after the SvREADONLY call `scalar(@a)` stops answering the count.  The
emitted form is `(Internals::pl-SvREADONLY @a 1)` -- an ordinary sub CALL -- not
the `Internals::SvREADONLY` MACRO whose docstring in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp
(`%p-array-set-readonly`, task #159) says "the caller ... stores the result back
into the variable's cell -- which is why the macro needs the variable, not its
value".  Start by finding out which of the two paths actually runs for this
spelling: the macro may simply not be reached, in which case the array keeps its
adjustable storage AND something else answers `scalar` wrongly.

The write side is RIGHT either way (`push` after the call dies "Modification of
a read-only value" in both engines), which is why no baseline row moved.
subject: Internals::SvREADONLY(@a,1) leaves scalar(@a) reading the ELEMENTS, not the count (pre-existing)
